clue.text: Last to come to the fore, is obsequious — that's hard to make out

indicators.text: Last to come to the fore
indicators.note: the final letter of the synonym is lifted from the back and set at the very front

parts.note: to crawl is to fawn or grovel, so he crawls

explanation.surface: A fawning latecomer pushes to the front, but what he says or writes is hard to decipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Untidy handwriting that is barely legible is a scrawl, a noun for illegible writing.

clue.text: Rather poor show, tame

indicators.note: a poor performance is a botched one, so these letters are botched into a new order

explanation.surface: A critic pans a rather dull, tame performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs of degree meaning to some extent, as in 'a bit tired'.

clue.text: Determined work on footwear, extremely urgent, inside

indicators.note: the two letters are placed within the cobbling word

parts.note: to resole a shoe is to fit it with a new sole, a cobbler's repair

indicators.note: takes just the two extreme letters, first and last, of the word urgent

explanation.surface: A cobbler sets about repairing shoes with grim determination because the job is urgent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone determined is firm of purpose and unwavering, the adjective meaning resolved.

clue.text: How mobile phone network ultimately gives period of time

indicators.note: takes the closing letter of each of the four words in turn

explanation.surface: A question about how a mobile network delivers some span of time, like a billing period.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven days make one of these calendar units, a standard span of time.

clue.text: Was equal of wine in exotic villa? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: signals one piece sitting within another
reverses the stated containment, so the wine wraps around the scrambled villa instead

parts.note: red is the everyday name for red wine

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and foreign, so these letters are made strange

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a wine served in a foreign villa could match another, only to be told the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the opposite' flips 'wine in villa': the villa, shuffled by 'exotic', holds nothing; instead the wine wraps around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rival something is to match it or equal it, so the past tense means matched.

clue.text: Unlucky, questionable, as leader is replaced — popular previously

indicators.note: puts the popular word before the rest

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular, as in 'the in crowd'

indicators.note: the opening letter of the doubtful word is swapped for another letter

parts.note: something suspicious is doubtful or questionable

indicators.note: the first letter of the word as

explanation.surface: A questionable, unlucky leader is replaced by a more popular predecessor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as leader is replaced' means the doubtful word's own first letter gives way to the leading letter of 'as'; 'popular previously' then puts the fashionable word in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Inauspicious means ill-omened, promising bad fortune, hence unlucky.

clue.text: Aren't clean at work? Regular change needed

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being rearranged into new positions

explanation.surface: Workers who aren't clean at work need a regular change of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternance is the regular alternation of two things, a periodic switching back and forth.

clue.text: Writer playing a prank? Not entirely

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: larking about is fooling or playing pranks

explanation.surface: A question whether some writer is only partly joking.
explanation.walkthrough: Philip Larkin was an English poet, famous for 'This Be The Verse'.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin, the English poet and novelist, is an example of a writer.

clue.text: Daughter and German seen ignoring outsiders in port

parts.note: und is the German word for and

indicators.note: drops the outer letters of the word seen, keeping its middle

explanation.surface: A daughter and a German are spotted in a port, but the outsiders are ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: Dundee is a port city on the east coast of Scotland, on the Firth of Tay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dundee is a Scottish harbour city on the Tay estuary, so an example of a port.

clue.text: Need to conceal knife outside as weapon

indicators.note: the necessity word wraps around and hides the other letters

parts.note: a must is something needed, an essential

indicators.note: keeps only the outside letters, first and last, of the word knife

explanation.surface: Someone needs to hide a knife outdoors to serve as a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A musket is an old smoothbore shoulder firearm, an example of a weapon.

clue.text: Absolutely reliable cold wine initially ready, or not?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

indicators.note: takes the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Is the cold wine ready yet, or not? A reliable host wants to know.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast-iron guarantee is one that cannot fail, like the rigid metal, hence absolutely dependable.

clue.text: As jet leg might see tradition upset

indicators.note: upset things are knocked over and jumbled, so these letters are tumbled

explanation.surface: Long-haul travel's jet lag throws a traveller's routines and traditions into disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg' is presumably meant as 'lag' (or a leg of a flight): jet lag is what leaves travellers confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet lag confuses the body clock, and to disorientate is to make someone lose their bearings.

clue.text: Bolt's smooth progress on return

indicators.note: the progress word is turned around and read backwards

parts.note: a flow is a steady, smooth movement onward

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt's smooth running form on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like the sprinter's name; here it is the verb meaning to gobble food.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt food is to gulp it down greedily, as does to wolf it.

clue.text: Don't expect action to follow this cheek at religious event

definitions.text: Don't expect action to follow this

parts.note: lip is impudent talk, insolence or cheek
a church service is an act of worship

explanation.surface: A warning about cheeky behaviour at a church event, where nothing will be done about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying mere verbal support to something without any intention of acting on it is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Politician, changing sides, absorbing the French tirade patiently

indicators.note: the altered politician word takes the other letters inside it
swaps right for left, R for L, within the politician word

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
le is French for the
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: A politician defects to the other party, sitting through a French tirade with forbearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing sides' turns the R (right) in TORY into L (left), giving TOLY, which absorbs LE and RANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with forbearance and without complaint is to behave patiently, putting up with things.

clue.text: Giant sail — can't moor unfortunately

indicators.note: an unlucky mishap sends these letters awry

explanation.surface: A huge sail on a ship that, sadly, cannot be tied up in harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomical means enormous, as large as the distances in space, hence giant.

clue.text: No drudge at work — little fellow

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being rearranged into new positions

explanation.surface: The small man at the office is no drudge.
explanation.definitionFit: The underdog is the one expected to lose, the little guy against the mighty, so a little fellow.

clue.text: Punishment? "Offenders will be fined" maybe

definitions.meaning: a penalty passed by a court on a convicted person
that quotation is an example of a grammatical unit of words with subject and verb

explanation.surface: A notice warning that offenders will be fined, raising the question of punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's penalty and a grammatical string of words are both named by the same word.

clue.text: Anecdote about cars, churches, entertaining knight

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Minis are the classic small British cars

indicators.note: the church letters host the knight between them

parts.note: CE, the Church of England, twice over
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A story about cars and churches with a knight as guest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a classic small British car; CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A recollection told as a story of past experience is a fond memory or anecdote.

clue.text: Glad war ends bringing ideas for spending?

indicators.note: the words carry the answer within them, across their boundaries

explanation.surface: People glad the war has ended plan what to spend money on.
explanation.walkthrough: Adware is software that shows advertisements, which suggest things to buy.
explanation.definitionFit: Software that pushes advertising is full of suggestions on what to buy, the question mark flagging the cryptic sense.

clue.text: Liveliness of sense regularly associated with pair, Italian

indicators.note: takes every other letter of the word sense, the even ones

parts.note: It is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A lively sense of fun is shared by two people and an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is spirited wit and vivacity, from the French for mind or spirit.

clue.text: Scorning girl, immoral, after lawyer intervenes

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: the lawyer comes between letters of the immoral word

parts.note: sinful means wicked or immoral
DA is a district attorney, a US prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A scornful girl is called immoral after a lawyer steps in.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing contempt and looking down on someone is to be scornful, the sense of scorning.

clue.text: Trial game

definitions.meaning: a check or examination to see how something performs
an international match in cricket or rugby

explanation.definitionFit: A trial or exam shares its name with an international cricket match between nations.

clue.text: Party men creating opening

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Men at a party make the first move.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged panel closing an entrance, the way in to a room, is an opening.

clue.text: City's aim, after review, to accommodate Republican leader

indicators.note: the rearranged letters house the Republican letter
reviewed letters are revised, so the aim word is rearranged

parts.note: three letters to be scrambled
a tsar was a Russian ruler, now any powerful leader

explanation.surface: A city's goals, once reviewed, must make room for a Republican leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after review' rearranges AIM into AMI, which takes in R to make AMRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Amritsar is a city in the Punjab, India, home to the Golden Temple.

clue.text: Very wet turf where animal lives

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a den is a wild animal's lair

explanation.surface: Waterlogged grass where some creature has its home.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaked through, saturated with water, is to be soggy and drenched.

clue.text: Newly housing female, eye rent payment

indicators.note: the scrambled letters hold the female letter within
these letters are made anew, put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new tenant, a woman, eyes the rent as payment.
explanation.definitionFit: The charge paid to be admitted to an event or competition is an admission charge, a kind of payment.

clue.text: Capital parking — argue slight change needed

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

indicators.note: the letters of argue are slightly altered in their order

explanation.surface: Parking in the capital city: argue for a slight change in the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Prague is the seat of government of the Czech Republic, so a capital city.
